ai.description: *Amolops assamensis* is a medium-sized frog (4–5 cm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale venter. It features a distinct white upper lip stripe and expanded, adhesive discs on the fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops assamensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored line running along the upper lip, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Amolops assamensis* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within subtropical evergreen forests, typically found at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Assamese Cascade Frog is primarily nocturnal, utilizing its specialized toe pads to cling to slippery, fast-flowing rocks while hunting for insects near mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops assamensis* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in streams. It breeds during the monsoon season, typically laying small clutches attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops assamensis* is endemic to Northeast India, specifically found in the states of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh within the Himalayan foothills and Brahmaputra basin.
ai.callDescription: The Assamese Cascade Frog produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps or whistles, typically heard while perched on mossy rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
